newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Yates apologises about beef comments.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Yates apologises about beef comments.

text.p: Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates on Thursday apologised to parliament for misleading comments about his handling of a deal which stopped exports of beef from three Irish counties to Russia.
"If I created a misleading impression then I apologise for that. I may have unwittingly misled Deputies on this subject," Yates said.

Ireland signed a deal last week stopping exports from three counties to Russia because of Russian fears about mad cow disease. Yates said he was forced to agree to the deal because Russia had threatened to ban all Irish beef.

Opposition parties on Thursday accused Yates of deliberately misleading the public over the circumstances of the deal's signing. They said he had implied he signed it personally at Dublin airport, when in fact he was not at the airport and officials signed it on his behalf.
Yates said he had never sought to pretend he had been present at the signing. He said he stood by the deal, which has provoked fury among farmers and opposition MPs.
Earlier, opposition leader Bertie Ahern said Yates should be sacked.

Ahern asked Yates in parliament if he had agreed to the ban "on an ultimatum from three Russian vets over the telephone". He wanted to know where Yates was during the negotiations and who he had consulted.
"An inexperienced minister does not make these kind of decisions on his own without the prime minister's knowledge and backing. If he did, he should be sacked," Ahern said.
